Jordan, Vanessa —

Below are the concise technical responses for the rows you flagged. I'm keeping the answers focused (Q12/Q15/Q18) and attaching small artifacts you can consume immediately. Happy to expand if you need more detail.

Q12 — KV cache & memory boundaries
- We maintain per-request/per-session KV caches scoped to the model session handle. KV cache memory is allocated from per-container GPU memory regions; sessions run inside isolated processes (containerized) and do not share pointers across tenant boundaries.
- Implementation: each model session gets a unique CUDA context isolated by the driver; shared CUDA IPC is not enabled between tenant sessions on Dedicated pools.
- Evidence: attached kvcache-isolation-snippet.txt contains a runtime log showing session id -> GPU allocation map; scheduler-audit-snapshot.log contains an excerpt of eviction events (timestamped) that demonstrate per-session eviction.

Q15 — Scheduling, eviction, and noisy-neighbor mitigation
- Dedicated pools are implemented as tenant-bound partitions. The scheduler enforces strict slot quotas (GPU-duty slots) and uses continuous batching within the slot to improve efficiency. If a slot exceeds its memory threshold or sustained latency deviation, we trigger an eviction + reinitialize flow for that session (graceful checkpoint).
- We also cap concurrent active contexts per GPU to prevent context thrashing and enforce soft CPU-level cgroups that limit host-side IO interference.
- For noisy-neighbor detection we run lightweight telemetry (per-context GPU SM utilization, memory bandwidth, latency percentiles). Alerts auto-generate a diagnostic bundle and escalate to an ops workflow for immediate remediation.

Q18 — Hardware-level separation for Dedicated pools
- Dedicated pools are provisioned onto isolated GPU nodes (no overcommit of model execution slots across tenants). We tag instances in our inventory so that dedicated nodes are never used for shared-host workloads.
- Where supported by the cloud instance, NVLink is used inside the node for multi-GPU models; cross-tenant NVLink sharing is disabled.

Artifacts attached: kvcache-isolation-snippet.txt (runtime allocation excerpt), scheduler-audit-snapshot.log (eviction/diag logs).

If you want, we can produce a short canary plan that intentionally runs a high-load noisy-job in an isolated test tenant so you can see the detection/eviction path and tail-latency impact.

Jordan —

Great questions. Short answers and next steps:

1) Benchmark snapshot: we will generate a p50/p95/p99 CSV from our internal noisy-neighbor run earlier this quarter and drop it in the Drive by EOD Dec 5. That snapshot includes baseline vs synthetic noisy-job run on an identically provisioned dedicated pool.

2) Canary plan: we have a 6-step plan with explicit metrics and rollback criteria. I created a draft in the Drive: "Canary-Plan-AcmeCloud.md" — please review and comment. Proposed window: Dec 9–10 (US PST hours) — we can compress to a 2-hour focused window if you prefer.

3) Persistent cross-tenant memory pressure: not expected in Dedicated pools because model weights are loaded per-node and we do not overcommit GPU memory. Edge case: very large pinned host-level model shards can increase host memory pressure; detection is via our telemetry (host memory + device memory correlation alerts). Mitigation: throttle new load, trigger a controlled eviction, and optionally migrate the tenant to a larger node.
